A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Reflection-Window Decoding and contain the main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison, including the reformatted appendix examples.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original decoding experiments on MT-Bench and MMLU. Appendices B–C include sensitivity analyses, regeneration measurements, generated examples, and subject-level results.

after.justification: Version 3 retains the original MT-Bench and MMLU experiments, together with the empirical analyses, examples, and detailed results in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 5.1 retain the same sliding reflection window, entropy-based pausing criterion, and fixed-length beam-search regeneration. No algorithmic component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MMLU subjects and MT-Bench tasks, including the same generation-history scenarios in Section 4 and the same appendix examples. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain greedy decoding, beam search, and Top-k/Top-p sampling. 'Full-scale' beam search is renamed 'vanilla' beam search with finite width; the newly cited decoding methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The benchmark metrics, GPT-4o response-order control, beam width 4 in Section 5.2, and decoding hyperparameters remain unchanged. Section 4 newly specifies settings for the existing sanity check, without establishing a revision to that experiment.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendix B retain the same window-size and entropy-threshold analyses, regeneration measurements, and three MT-Bench case studies. The redesigned and reordered examples provide no new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the twice-per-pair, order-reversed judging procedure remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–15 and the quantitative plots retain their results. For example, Table 1 still reports macro accuracies of 78.14%, 76.44%, and 78.15% for greedy, beam, and reflection-window decoding. The reformatted appendix examples preserve the same generated responses.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.2, Assumptions 3.3–3.5, Theorem 3.6, and the Appendix A proof are unchanged. The added theoretical remark explains the existing result without modifying its mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about autoregressive suboptimality, selective refinement, and performance relative to existing decoding approaches.

C2.justification: A new remark following Theorem 3.6 explicitly describes the oracle assumption as unrealistic in practice and states that the empirical evaluations do not rely on it. A new Section 5.2 footnote clarifies finite-width beam search versus unconstrained exhaustive search.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly identifies Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and beam width 10 for the existing Figure 4 sanity check. These previously unspecified details improve reproducibility documentation without demonstrating that the experiment changed.

R1.justification: The introduction and references add Shih et al.'s Long Horizon Temperature Scaling and Li et al.'s Contrastive Decoding. This modestly expands the discussion of temperature adjustment and optimization using multiple models while preserving the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Version 3 adds limited explanatory passages and terminology edits, updates author order and publication text, and reorders and retitles the acknowledgment and impact sections. The main section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 7–9 are substantially redesigned from compact side-by-side response panels into separate pages with larger, vertically stacked, distinctly colored panels and explicit headers. The story and shadow examples exchange Figure 8/9 positions. Figure 3 and Table 1 move, and Figure 5 gains a clearer comparison caption.

improvement.justification: Version 3 improves reproducibility by specifying the sanity-check model and beam width, clarifies the relationship between theoretical assumptions and empirical evaluation, and makes the appendix examples substantially easier to read. These are useful but limited overall gains; the method, formal results, experimental coverage, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
